summary: Chlodwig H. Werba is an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He held a post as Prof. Dr. at the University of Vienna, attested between 1990 and 2006, and again in 2022.
Chogye Shabdrung works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sakya College in 2003 under Khenchen Sonam Gyatso.

Chogye Trichen Rinpoche worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kunga Chophel, Geshe Tsechok (1929), Zimwok Rinpoche, and the 13th Dalai Lama, and served as the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Phenpo Nalendra Monastery from 1928.
Chogyū Takayama worked in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Fukushima Prefectural Asaka High School around 1887 to 1890 and at the University of Tokyo around 1893 to 1896.
Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, whom he also taught.
Chong Go is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University and under Daehaeng (attested in 2012).
Chris Clark specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Sydney by 2015 under Mark Allon and served there as an honorary associate, attested in 2019.
Chris Williams works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Attested in 2026, he studied at the University of Bristol as an MPhil and PhD student and teaching staff member under Rita Langer.

Christiaan Hooykaas specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Leiden University (1921–1929, PhD) under Jean Philippe Vogel. He was acting Professor at the University of Indonesia (1946) and Lecturer at SOAS University of London (1951–1953).

Christiaan Snouck Hurgronje studied at the Nederlands-Indische Bestuursacademie, Leiden University (c. 1874–1880), and under Theodor Nöldeke (c. 1880–1881). He held posts at Leiden University (1887, 1889–1890, 1906–1927) and the Oostersch Genootschap in Nederland (c. 1920–1921).

Christian August Brandis was a philosopher and historian. He studied at Kiel University (c. 1808–1812) and held academic posts at the University of Copenhagen (c. 1812–1815), Humboldt University of Berlin (c. 1816–1821), and the University of Bonn (c. 1821–1867).

Christian Bartholomae studied at Munich, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Leipzig (PhD 1872–1878) under Curtius, Zarncke, Brockhaus, Hübschmann, and von Spiegel. He held professorships at Halle-Wittenberg (1879, 1884), Münster (1885–1898), Giessen (1898–1909), Strasbourg (1909), and Heidelberg (1909–1924).

Christian Bernert works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, Junjie Chu, Karin Preisendanz, and Gerald Hödl.

Christian Charles Josias von Bunsen studied at Marburg, Göttingen under C.G. Heyne, Munich, Leiden, Copenhagen, and under Silvestre de Sacy. He served as Prussian envoy (c. 1823–1854) and founded the German Archaeological Institute (1829).

Christian Coseru studied at the University of Bucharest and Australian National University (PhD c. 1998–2003). He has held positions at the College of Charleston (c. 2006) and the University of California, Berkeley (2017).

Christian Ferstl works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna, held a lectorate there in 2014, and worked as a research project collaborator at the University of Leipzig in 2021.

Christian Gilberti works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley, where he served as a Graduate Student Representative (attested 2026) and held a post in South and Southeast Asian Studies.

Christian Gottlob Heyne studied at the University of Leipzig (1748–1752). He served as Professor der Beredsamkeit und Dichtkunst at the University of Göttingen from 1763 and as Director of the Göttingen State and University Library from 1764 to 1812.

Christian Haskett specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2010), having studied with Robert A. F. Thurman and Michael Witzel, and held a post at Washington and Lee University.

Christian K. Wedemeyer earned his MA and PhD at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman. He held posts at Antioch University, New College of Florida, the University of Copenhagen (2000–2003), and the University of Chicago (2003–2011).
